clue.text: Luvvies left off wrecking American hot spot

indicators.note: wrecking smashes the remaining letters and puts them together in a new order
something left off is taken away, so the L goes from the word luvvies

explanation.surface: Thespians are wreaking havoc at some fashionable American venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Luvvies' are luvvie actors on the surface. 'left off' removes L; 'wrecking' then rearranges UVVIES into VESUVI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian volcano is literally a hot spot, a place where molten rock breaks through.

clue.text: Food for half a dozen adders

parts.note: half a dozen is six, VI in Roman numerals
the word 'and' adds one thing to another, so 'ands' are adders

explanation.surface: A suggestion of what to feed six snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: Adders look like snakes, but here they are things that add, the conjunction AND in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Viands is an old word for items of food, especially fine fare.

clue.text: A lot of filth by leader of Lords causes brief storm

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, means some letters are cut from the end of the synonym for filth

parts.note: squalor is filth and wretched dirt

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Lords

explanation.surface: Dirt left by a peer's chief prompts a short-lived uproar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims OR from SQUALOR, leaving SQUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A squall is a sudden violent gust of wind, a short burst of stormy weather.

clue.text: Small book on small boats — there are six in the puzzle

definitions.text: there are six in the puzzle

parts.note: VOL, short for volume, is a book made small by abbreviation
canoes are small light boats

explanation.surface: A slim volume about little craft, set among other puzzle themes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link in this down clue. The definition refers to the six volcanoes themed across the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The grid holds six fire-mountains: Vesuvius, Stromboli, Etna, St Helens, Erebus and Krakatoa.

clue.text: Outlines tend to be blurred or ignored

indicators.note: letters that are blurred lose their shape and come out in a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Sketchy outlines tend to go unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be blurred' rearranges OUTLINES and TEND; 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not listened to is disregarded, the same as being ignored.

clue.text: See 23
Course of salts

definitions.meaning: a racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby
magnesium sulphate crystals used as a purgative, named after a Surrey spring

explanation.surface: A course of medicinal salts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like a course of treatment, but it is the racecourse; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is both a famous English racecourse and the name of a well-known purgative salt.

clue.text: Type of order sent with letter

definitions.meaning: a religious order whose members live shut away from the world
put in the same envelope as a letter

explanation.surface: An order sent by post with a covering letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Enclosed describes cloistered religious communities and also items put in with a letter.

clue.text: Monarch in 20 finds stalk with spores

indicators.note: in places the monarch inside the answer to the other clue

parts.note: the answer to 20-down, a mark of disgrace
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A king inside a mark discovers a stalk bearing spores.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany a sterigma is a small stalk on a fungus that bears spores.

clue.text: Marking "Funny Girl" "For adults only" is a bloomer

parts.note: A was the old British film certificate for adult audiences
rum means odd or funny
Lily is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Rating the musical Funny Girl as adults-only would be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marking' means labelling with the old A film certificate, which goes in front. A bloomer is a blunder on the surface but a flower here.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum lily is a flowering plant, so in crosswordese it is a bloomer.

clue.text: The soul of a tipsy cherub

indicators.note: of says the answer is drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Spirituality found in a drunken little angel.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyche is the Greek word for the soul or mind.

clue.text: Barnard, say, prepares expat for growing tea, say, when I leave

indicators.note: when I leaves, the letter I is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: trains means prepares
a planter was a colonial settler running a tea or rubber plantation

explanation.surface: A surgeon readies a colonial for cultivating crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when I leave' removes I from TRAINS, leaving TRANS. Christiaan Barnard did the first human heart transplant.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnard was a surgeon who moved hearts between patients, an example of one who transplants.

clue.text: Letter to 14 towards the end

definitions.meaning: the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet
the last word of 14-across is a river, and the river's mouth is where it ends

explanation.surface: Write to 14 near the close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. The second definition points at STREAM, the end of 14-across, and a delta is the stream near its end.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is a Greek letter and also the fan of land where a river reaches the sea.

clue.text: Second instrument with the wrong half line in Italian island

indicators.note: the wrong half of the instrument is swapped out for something else

parts.note: the trombone is a brass instrument

indicators.note: half takes the first two letters of line

explanation.surface: A second brass player is out of line on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with the wrong' replaces NE, the last half of TROMBONE, with LI, half of 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stromboli is a small volcanic island off the north coast of Sicily.

clue.text: Words to encourage new master to start working

parts.note: come on is said to urge someone forward

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of master take a fresh order

explanation.surface: Encouragement given to a new boss on day one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns MASTER into STREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: When a plant or project comes on stream it begins operating.

clue.text: Retreats make Spooner set fire to hay

indicators.note: Spooner, the Oxford don, swaps the opening sounds of words

parts.note: burn means set fire to
a stack is a pile of hay

explanation.surface: Withdrawals cause a reverend to torch the haystack.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the B and T sounds of BURN STACK gives 'turn sback', said as TURNS BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to turn back, giving up ground.

clue.text: Novel lodging kept by a lady

indicators.note: kept by means held inside the following words

parts.note: a dame is a lady, often titled
a bed is a place to lodge for the night

explanation.surface: A woman offers rooms in her house.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Bede is George Eliot's first novel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a novel by George Eliot, published in 1859.

clue.text: Composer, namely Parry?

parts.note: sc, scilicet, means namely
Sir Hubert Parry was an English composer

explanation.surface: A request to identify a composer as Parry.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Parry gives only his first name, HUBERT. Parry was himself a composer, so the surface reads as a tidy answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Schubert was the Austrian composer of lieder and symphonies.

clue.text: Peace pledger, not nail blower, for ship, deck being arranged by mate

indicators.note: arranged letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: pard is an old slang word for a partner or mate

explanation.surface: A pacifist, not a shepherd, rearranges a ship's deck with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being arranged' turns SHIP DECK into DICKSHEP. 'not nail blower' rules out Dick the shepherd, who 'blows his nail' in the song from Love's Labour's Lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Canon Dick Sheppard founded the Peace Pledge Union in the 1930s.

clue.text: Bird, very first model as jazz musician

indicators.note: first says the abbreviation for very goes at the front

parts.note: the ibis is a wading bird
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A bird stands as the earliest form of jazz player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts V before IBIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A vibist plays the vibraphone, a staple of jazz.

clue.text: Backward idiots get half mark, a black one

indicators.note: backward means the synonym for idiots is read from right to left

parts.note: gits is British slang for idiots

indicators.note: half takes the first two letters of mark

explanation.surface: Slow fools earn only half marks, and black ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' turns GITS into STIG. 'one' stands for mark, so the definition is 'a black mark'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, a black mark against someone.

clue.text: Return of money staked on horse in Italian island

indicators.note: on in an across clue sets the turned stake after the horse word

parts.note: a mount is a horse for riding

indicators.note: return means the stake word is turned back to front

parts.note: an ante is a stake in poker

explanation.surface: Getting back a bet placed on a horse in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: Etna is not an island itself, so the definition reads 'in Italian island': the volcano stands in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Etna is the volcano that stands in Sicily.

clue.text: The first relative to bait?

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of The

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: Is the first relative there to torment someone?
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt is to tease or provoke, just as to bait is.

clue.text: It's in the glass where it was made

definitions.text: It's in the glass where it was made

parts.words: It's in the glass where it was made
parts.note: an American volcano named after a Lancashire town famous for glassmaking

explanation.surface: A thing seen in glass from the place that produced it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Pilkington glass works are in the town in Merseyside; the volcano in Washington state shares its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The volcano's name is the name of an English town where glass is made.

clue.text: It was hell before transport came

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a bus is a form of transport

explanation.surface: Life was miserable before buses came along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came' is a link. Erebus is also a volcano in Antarctica, one of the puzzle's six.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the darkness of the underworld, a region of Hades.

clue.text: Theft from canonized studio

parts.note: a canonized person is a saint, ST
Ealing Studios in London made famous British comedies

explanation.surface: Something nicked from a saintly film studio.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the act of theft, taking what is not yours.

clue.text: A lot of houses and a car

definitions.meaning: a British word for a station wagon

explanation.surface: A lot of houses and a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link. An estate car, or estate, is the British name for a station wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: Estate means a housing development and also a long-backed car.

clue.text: After-dinner noise maker heard getting to a Pacific island

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: a Christmas cracker bangs at the end of dinner
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bangers heard at the end of dinner lead to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link. Krakatoa erupted catastrophically in 1883.
explanation.definitionFit: Krakatoa is a volcanic island in Indonesia, between Java and Sumatra.
